findings.title: Same will, harsher outcome
findings.claim: The second يَشَأْ repeats the same jussive will before the Form II punishment verb; the outcome grows morphologically heavier while the will predicate stays unchanged.
findings.mechanism: The focus pairs the repeated Form I will form with a distinct Form II outcome, placing the added form-weight on punishment rather than on willing.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the contrast without turning the second outcome into a stronger or more certain act of willing.
findings.containment: The local verbal contrast preserves both conditional outcomes and does not say which occurs.

epistemic.reason: Exact focus morphology and the repeated aligned will form support the bounded comparison.

findings.title: Second jussive will
findings.claim: The second will verb remains jussive under its own conditional particle, so punishment is presented as contingent under the same recoverable divine subject as mercy.
findings.mechanism: The second إِن governs the aligned يَشَأْ and its jussive form; its relation to the first matching condition gives the punishment arm its own suspended gate.
findings.reader_payoff: Punishment is not the inevitable next step after mercy is named.
findings.containment: This states the local conditional grammar and leaves both possible outcomes open.

epistemic.reason: The supplied QAC alignment and attachment evidence identify the second protasis and jussive verb.

findings.title: Punishment as second answer
findings.claim: يُعَذِّبْكُمْ answers the second conditional and directs its punishment to the same plural addressees carried through the ayah.
findings.mechanism: The second apodosis supplies the result of the second إن and its attached plural suffix marks the audience as direct object.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees a complete second possibility aimed at the same people, not a detached description of punishment.
findings.containment: The clause names a possible answer under the condition; it does not assign the outcome to a group.

epistemic.reason: Attachment and QAC evidence identify the second apodosis and its object suffix.

findings.title: Form II weight

findings.mechanism: The local pair places the less-doubled mercy form beside a morphologically intensified punishment form, so sound and form distinguish the two outcomes.
findings.reader_payoff: The contrast is audible in the verbs themselves, not only in the translated labels.
findings.containment: This is a local formal contrast; it does not make punishment more certain or decide between the alternatives.

epistemic.reason: QAC morphology and the directly paired focus verbs support the form and sound relation.

epistemic.reason: Each focus relation is explicit, while their whole-ayah integration is an interpretive synthesis.
